newsitem.title: UK: Italy minister says Commission comment appropriate.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister says Commission comment appropriate.

text.p: Italian Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi on Monday said European Commission criticism of spending controls in 1996 was appropriate and added that Brussels was being co-operative with Rome.
Earlier the Commission was quoted as criticising current control of general government expenditure but it later transpired that it had been refering to 1996 accounts.
"If that is the case, then everything is back to normal and the Commission comments are appropriate," Fantozzi told reporters during a visit to the Italian trade board in Britain.
"I have always thought there was a totally co-operative atmosphere (between Italy and the Commission)," he added.

Italy overshot 1996 spending targets and finished with a deficit to gross domestic product ratio of 6.7 percent. It has pledged to bring this down to three percent in 1997 to meet one of the critieria in the Maastricht Treaty for EMU hopefuls. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
